title: Home
text:
Welcome to my portfolio for MUSA 5080: Public Policy Analytics at the University of Pennsylvania.
This site documents my work in the Master of Urban Spatial Analytics program — weekly notes, course assignments, and a final project applying data analysis to urban policy questions.


Hi! I’m a student in the MUSA program at Penn. My background is in GIS, and I’m interested in GIS.




Weekly Notes — what I’m learning each week
Assignments — analyses completed for the course

What is a website?

title: About
text: Before MUSA, I did a couple different things. I was a part of NASA DEVELOP where I conducted a spatial and temporal analysis of landfill methane emissions in New Hampshire. I also worked for the DC Govt. where I helped manage their database systems (enterprise and through GitHub and ArcGIS). I did a recent project for Mapping Black California where I rebuilt their Stop the Hate Dashboard that helps users identify hate crime patterns across California based on demographic and time. Right now, I help Spectrum (Charter Communications) map rural America and their internet serviceability. I became interested in Urban Spatial Analytics when I took an applied Social Statistics class where I could gather public data and make meaningful analyses with it. I hope to continue that throughout and after MUSA.

title: Week 2
text:
verbs

filter(): picks rows
select(): picks columns
mutate(): add a new computed column
arrange(): change the order of rows (asc, desc)
group_by() + summarize(): many rows become few

Step 1.
filter(counties, moe_pct>10)
Step 2.
arrange(Step1, desc(moe_pct))
Step 3.
select(NAME, moe_pct)

Want to write “and then”?

%>% or |> : strings functions without saving an intermediate file along the way like steps 1-3.


Steps 1-3 become:
new_data ← counties %>%
    filter(moe_pct) %>%
    arrange(desc(moe_pct))%>%
    select(NAME, moe_pct)
takes input (counties) and applies these functions at once into a single

title: Week 2
text:
census data
Decennial Census

10 years
10 questions
long form

American Community Survey (ACS)

2005
3% of households are surveyed on income, commute, ethnicity, rent, etc..
Results in an estimate for the population
1-year ACS conducted in places > 65,000 people (data available and current at metropolitan level)
5-year ACS (block groups and census tracts)

each year represents a 5-year average
estimate +- a margin of error (MOE)


B1234_001E
B is the Base table
1234 is the table number
001E is the Line number
E is the Estimate
M is the MOE
load_variables()
state → county → tract (neighborhood of 5-8,000 people and boundaries change frequently)
GEOID
42101000100
42 is the state
101 is the county
000100 is the tract (11 digits)
block groups is the 12th

always stored as string
make sure u check the way its stored before trying to do anything with it
